clue.text: A hard back

parts.note: stern means hard, severe

explanation.surface: Reads like a terse description of something with a hard back, a book perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship, astern is an adverb meaning backwards or towards the rear, so it can stand for 'back'.

clue.text: Start to doctor a sea inlet, possibly

definitions.text: Start to doctor a sea inlet, possibly

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so only the opening letter of doctor is used
possibly signals that the letters of a sea inlet may be arranged in another way

explanation.surface: Suggests treating the salty water of a sea inlet as the first step in doctoring it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges A SEA INLET into ESALINATE, after the D from 'Start to doctor'. The whole clue also describes the process.
explanation.definitionFit: Removing salt is the first thing done to make seawater from an inlet drinkable, so the whole clue describes the process.

clue.text: Insect, note, coming on board in small quantities

indicators.note: coming on board a ship means getting inside it, so these letters go inside the ship's letters

parts.note: on board means aboard a ship; SS (steamship) stands for the vessel that is boarded
a midge is a small biting insect

explanation.surface: An insect and a note get on board, in small amounts, like a stowaway story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is the crossword convention for going inside SS, the steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: A smidgen is a tiny amount, so the plural means small quantities.

clue.text: Film workers, say, heading off, about to challenge critic's response

indicators.note: about says the remaining letters go around the next piece
the heading of a word is its first letter, which comes off here

parts.note: a film crew is the team of workers on a shoot
to vie is to compete or challenge

explanation.surface: Film workers set out to challenge a critic's verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film workers, say' is a crew, the 'say' flagging an example rather than a definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A review is the written assessment a critic gives of a film, book or show.

clue.text: Sleepy, having lost party sparkle

indicators.note: having lost says the next piece is taken away

parts.note: dozing means sleepy, nodding off
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Someone drowsy has lost the sparkle a party should give them.
explanation.definitionFit: Zing is liveliness or zest, the same quality as sparkle.

clue.text: Slips — or other lingerie items?

definitions.meaning: long loose knickers, women's underwear like slips

explanation.walkthrough: 'Slips' reads as underwear, but the first sense is mistakes; the second definition carries the underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloomers is British slang for blunders and also the name of old-fashioned loose knickers.

clue.text: Regarded swarm getting amongst scattered seed

indicators.note: getting amongst says one piece goes into the middle of the other
scattered seed is spread out, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: to teem is to swarm, be full of

explanation.surface: A swarm of birds descends on seed scattered on the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regarded' looks like a verb in the past tense meaning looked at; here it means held in regard.
explanation.definitionFit: Esteemed means held in high regard, so it is a past participle like 'regarded'.

clue.text: Audacious US lawyer leading cartel

indicators.note: leading means this piece comes first, before the next

parts.note: DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecutor
a ring is a group working together illegally, like a cartel

explanation.surface: An American lawyer heading a cartel is bold indeed.
explanation.definitionFit: Daring and audacious are both adjectives for boldness that ignores risk.

clue.text: Religious text initially replaced by edition of consuming interest?

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter, which is replaced by the next piece

parts.note: the Bible is the religious text of Christianity

explanation.surface: A new edition of a sacred book is a matter of real interest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consuming' is literal: something that can be eaten is of interest to a consumer; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fit to eat is a pun on 'consuming interest', since it interests the one doing the consuming.

clue.text: Target of Zeus in fabled antiquity

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words fabled antiquity

explanation.surface: Zeus's conquest is the stuff of fabled ancient myth.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth, Zeus pursued and seduced Leda in the form of a swan.

clue.text: Delightful fashionable people in town

parts.note: darling means sweet or delightful
the ton is high society, fashionable people

explanation.surface: Charming, stylish people out on the town.
explanation.walkthrough: DARLINGTON is a market town in County Durham, north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a specific example of a town, named in a general way by the clue.

clue.text: Surfing, individual captures connection to another page, mostly

indicators.note: captures says the first piece holds the next one inside it

parts.note: one means a single individual

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: a link joins one web page to another

explanation.surface: A web user finds a link to another page while browsing.
explanation.definitionFit: Surfing the web means browsing it while connected to the internet.

clue.text: Unpleasant looks returned after City backed some reportage

indicators.note: after puts the reversed looks after the reversed city
backed means this word is read backwards

parts.note: a wen is a large crowded city; London was called the Great Wen

indicators.note: returned means this word is read from the end back

parts.note: leers are sly, unpleasant looks

explanation.surface: Nasty looks come back after the City backs a piece of journalism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns WEN into NEW and 'returned' turns LEERS into SREEL. 'City' is the old London nickname 'the Great Wen'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cinema news film is a form of reportage, so it is 'some' of it.

clue.text: Dodgy item can't get carried by soldiers ready to be posted

indicators.note: get carried by says this piece goes inside the soldiers' letters

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or doubtful, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Soldiers lug around a shady item that can't be posted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' is British slang for cash, and the Royal Engineers are the soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: 'ready' is slang for money, and money sent by post is a payment sent off.

clue.text: Go by cathedral feature that's behind article from Gaudi?

indicators.note: that's behind puts the cathedral feature after the article

parts.note: el is 'the' in Spanish; Gaudi was a Spanish architect
an apse is the rounded end of a cathedral or church

explanation.surface: A tour passes by Gaudi's cathedral, perhaps the Sagrada Familia in Barcelona.
explanation.walkthrough: Gaudi stands for Spanish, so his article is EL.
explanation.definitionFit: Time going by is time that has passed, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Disordered atlas brought in final Oriental location

indicators.note: brought in says the rearranged letters go inside the other piece

parts.note: the final part of something is its end

indicators.note: disordered says the letters are out of order

explanation.surface: A messy atlas helps reach a last destination in the East.
explanation.definitionFit: An eastern land is a region of the Orient, so a location there.

clue.text: Morning, in the main, perhaps, will do for Irishman

indicators.note: in says the morning goes inside the waters

parts.note: the main is the open ocean; 'perhaps' marks it as an example of seas
AM, ante meridiem, means morning

explanation.surface: A morning at sea is just the thing for an Irishman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is the poetic name for the open ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Seamas is an Irish form of the forename James, so names a man from Ireland.

clue.text: The old getting upset about standard sexiness — that's something outrageous

indicators.note: about says the old word goes around the other pieces
in a down clue, upset means turned upside down

parts.note: ye is an old form of 'the'
a norm is a standard
it is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: An old person is upset about modern standards of sex appeal: it's an outrage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'IT' for sex appeal comes from the 1927 film 'It' with Clara Bow.
explanation.definitionFit: An enormity is an outrageous wickedness or monstrous act.

clue.text: Couples starting asking Theresa May, revealing complaint

indicators.note: couples means pairs, and starting means the first pair of letters from each of the next words

explanation.surface: Reporters asking Theresa May questions reveal a complaint against her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Couples starting' takes the opening two letters of each word: AS, TH, MA. Theresa May was British Prime Minister in 2019.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint can be an illness, and asthma is a chronic breathing illness.

clue.text: Happen to interrupt fool and drunk returning dangerous material?

indicators.note: to interrupt says this piece goes inside the next one

parts.note: an ass is a fool
to be is to happen, take place

indicators.note: returning means the word is read back to front

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard

explanation.surface: Something happens to break up a fool and a drunk on their way home.
explanation.definitionFit: This fibrous mineral is a known cancer risk, an example of a dangerous material.

clue.text: Cockney tough guy picked up in Arctic landscape

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means lifted, so read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a hard nut is a tough guy; a Cockney drops the H, so 'ard nut

explanation.surface: A tough Cockney is caught out in the Arctic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' tempts as a homophone, but here it lifts the letters: 'ARD NUT read upwards. Cockneys, from London's East End, drop their H's.
explanation.definitionFit: Tundra is the vast treeless plain of the Arctic with permanently frozen subsoil.

clue.text: Old bargain regarding bones

parts.note: a steal is something bought for very little, a bargain

explanation.surface: Looks like a dealer's note on an old bargain in the bone trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Osteal is a medical adjective meaning of or relating to bone.

clue.text: Times Editor's foremost among 25 fellers

indicators.note: among puts these letters inside the other piece

parts.note: this points to the answer of 25 across, the word said at the end of a prayer
X is the multiplication sign, meaning times

indicators.note: foremost means the front letter of this word

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor leads a team of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fellers' looks like slang for men, but it is those who fell trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumberjacks who chop trees down are fellers, those who fell.

clue.text: Town with unexpected Latin charm

indicators.note: unexpected says the letters come out in a surprising order

explanation.surface: A town has an unexpected Latin charm about it.
explanation.walkthrough: ALTRINCHAM is a town in Greater Manchester, England.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a specific example of a town in north-west England.

clue.text: Some European Government dismissed, causing stink

indicators.note: dismissed says the government letter is removed

parts.note: a Greek is one European

explanation.surface: A European government is sacked amid a political stink.
explanation.definitionFit: A reek is a strong unpleasant smell, the same as a stink.

clue.text: Monks, say, behind a termination of religious activity?

indicators.note: behind puts the monks after the a

parts.note: monks are an example of men

explanation.surface: Monks lagging behind signal the end of worship.
explanation.definitionFit: This word is said at the close of a prayer or hymn, ending an act of worship.

clue.text: Make valuable contribution to high-end earnings

indicators.note: contribution to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Reads like financial advice on boosting the top earners' income.
explanation.definitionFit: To make someone cherished or dear to others is to make them valued, valuable in affection.

clue.text: Movement in French city seen in newspaper items

indicators.note: seen in says this piece sits inside the French city

parts.note: Arles is a city in Provence, southern France
a tic is an involuntary twitch or movement

explanation.surface: A movement in a French city is reported in the papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Pieces of writing in a newspaper are called articles.
